Write M = 100A + 10B + C and N = 100D + 10E + F. By linearity,

E[MN] = Σ over position pairs (weight_i · weight_j) · E[X_i X_j],

where the X's are the six digits in their positions.

**Same-position terms.** E[X_i²] = (1+4+9+16+25+36)/6 = 91/6.

**Different-position terms.** For i ≠ j, E[X_i X_j] = (S² − Q)/(30), where S = 21 and Q = 91, so the sum over ordered pairs is 441 − 91 = 350. Dividing by the 30 ordered pairs gives 350/30 = 35/3.

**Weights.** M and N use the same weights w = (100, 10, 1), with the digit at position k of M paired against the digit at position l of N. All of these pairs are different digits, since A..F are six distinct positions. So every product w_k·w_l involves two distinct variables, and

E[MN] = (Σw)² · 35/3 = 111² · 35/3 = 12321 · 35/3 = 4107 · 35 = 143745.

Check: 4107 · 35 = 123210 + 20535 = 143745.

ANSWER: 143745
